function: PPO agent allocates DFT-codebook beams (keep, best, sweep, switch) to each user per TTI from sensing echoes and buffer states, trading communication latency against range and velocity estimation error (p. 7-8).
system: Mono-static OFDM ISAC BS, NT=16-antenna transmit ULA and NR-antenna receive ULA, U=2 single-antenna users, 28 GHz, DFT codebook; no RIS (p. 3, 9).
method: Reinforcement learning: PPO agent with fully connected policy network (2 hidden layers of 128 nodes), trained offline for 1.2 million steps; DQN, A2C, TD7 also tried (p. 10, 12).
data_channel: Self-built simulator: 100 m x 100 m road scene, two vehicles; LoS channel without clutter, Rician K=10 dB with four clutters; no standard or public dataset (p. 9).
test_conditions: Six sets of initial user positions for training, 500 test episodes from a disjoint set; clutter-free and cluttered channels; speeds 6-14 m/s, arrival probabilities 0.5-0.9 (p. 9-11).
baselines: Non-learned: X-TDMA (1/7/13/19), AoD-based MUSIC heuristic, Xie [15] CSI-based optimization, Genie upper bound. Learned: DQN, A2C, TD7; PPO-1b is a variant (p. 9-10).
metrics: Average reward, throughput CDF, average packet latency, probability that normalized range, velocity, and angle errors fall below 0.2 (p. 9-12).
complexity: Runtime order O(sum of n_{l-1} n_l) per TTI for the fully connected policy network (2 hidden layers of 128 nodes); no FLOPs or measured runtime (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 4: "The channel is assumed Rician with Rician K-factor"; custom simulator (p. 9: Rician K-factor of 10, four clutters), with no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 9: "During testing, 500 episodes are evaluated, each with user positions initialized randomly from a test set that is disjoint from the training set"; this is a held-out set of the same scenario, and no test under another scenario, number of users, or clutter layout than in training is described.
q3_support: p. 11: "The PPO-based method outperforms the AoD-based and X-TDMA methods"; p. 10: "PPO surpasses A2C after more than 12k training episodes"
q4_support: p. 12: "complexity of one TTI is O"; p. 12: "the implemented neural network has 2 hidden layers, each with 128 nodes"
q5_support: p. 9: "The simulation parameters are summarized in Table I"; the scenario is the authors' own simulation, and the paper gives no code or data link or DOI and uses no public or measured dataset.
notes: ris=0: the system has no RIS (p. 3). Step 1: the learned decision is the physical-layer beam allocation from a DFT codebook (p. 3, 8), with buffer states only as cross-layer input, so it is not above_phy; power allocation and the user priority on beam collisions are non-learned (p. 7-8). q2=0: the only unseen data is a disjoint set of initial positions of the same scenario (p. 9), and the sweeps over speed (Fig. 4) and arrival probability (Fig. 5c) are not stated to test an agent trained under other values. q3=1 is borderline: the learned baselines DQN, A2C, and TD7 are compared with PPO only on the training reward, which is the paper's latency-plus-sensing objective (Fig. 3, p. 10), while the non-learned baselines are compared on throughput, latency, and estimation errors (p. 11-12); PPO-1b is a variant and is not counted. The reviewer should confirm q3.
